title: An orphaned change is attributed and resolved, never left in the tree
intention: Every uncommitted change in either repo that no open ticket's build claims is named, attributed to the session that wrote it, and then either committed into its ticket or moved to the trash, never left lying silent in the tree.
traces_to: Law 5 (the repo is itself the state of the machine, and an orphan is state no record explains). Law 7 (an error stays loud: an orphan is named until resolved). Akien's 8u answer, 2026-10-07.
how: (a) bin/cmd/orphans, a python script in the bin/cmd style, with subcommands list (the default), adopt and remove. (b) The roots come from env CAIRN_ORPHANS_ROOTS (colon-separated, a fixture seam), defaulting to the two repos. The transcripts dir comes from CAIRN_ORPHANS_TRANSCRIPTS, defaulting to ~/.claude/projects. The trash goes through bin/cmd/trash with its own env seam. (c) The claimed set is the union of chain_for_ticket(t)['decompose'] sub_problems writes_to over open tickets, repo-relative, read with berths_root from CAIRN_ORPHANS_BERTHS for the fixture. (d) Attribution scans the transcripts newest-mtime-first and stops at the first tool_use naming the absolute path. (e) The proof is at the path above, five teeth, PROVES keyed on this ticket, and it builds its repos with git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t in a tempdir.
falsifier: Done when bin/proofs/test_orphans_are_attributed_and_resolved.py is green under bin/cairn test --netns. (1) In fixture repos, an open fixture ticket whose decompose claims a.py, with a.py and b.py both dirty: `orphans` lists b.py only. (2) A fixture transcript whose Write call names b.py attributes b.py to that session and timestamp. (3) `adopt b.py --ticket <id>` leaves b.py clean and HEAD's message names the id. (4) `remove` on an untracked c.py leaves it in the fixture trash and absent from the tree; on a modified tracked d.py it leaves a .patch in the trash and d.py at HEAD. (5) adopt of a claimed path, or under an unknown ticket id, refuses and writes nothing. Red at HEAD: no bin/cmd/orphans.
